Baal-shalisha
BAY-al-SHAL-ish-ah
proper noun
Hebrew ba‘al shālīshāh, “lord of Shalisha” or “place of the three,” a town in the land of Shalisha whence came a man with firstfruits unto Elisha.

📖 Biblical Definition

Baal-shalisha is a town in the land of Shalisha, the region through which Saul passed when he sought his father’s asses (1Sam 9:4), made memorable in the days of Elisha by a deed of the prophet’s power and the LORD’s provision. “And there came a man from Baal-shalisha, and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in the husk” (2Ki 4:42). When Elisha bade his servant set it before the hundred men of the sons of the prophets, the servant marvelled; but the prophet said, “Give the people, that they may eat: for thus saith the LORD, They shall eat, and shall leave thereof” (2Ki 4:43). “So he set it before them, and they did eat, and left thereof, according to the word of the LORD” (2Ki 4:44). Thus a man bringing the firstfruits of his ground unto the man of God became the occasion of a miracle of multiplied bread, a sign that went before the greater feeding which the Lord Jesus wrought with a few loaves. The name carries the dark sound of Baal, the false god whose worship was Israel’s plague; yet here a faithful man honoured the true God with his firstfruits, and the LORD honoured his gift with increase. Baal-shalisha witnesses that the LORD is no man’s debtor, and that the little brought to Him in faith He multiplies, so that many eat and are filled and there is yet to spare.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town in the land of Shalisha whence a man brought firstfruits to Elisha, who fed a hundred men.

expand to see more

BAAL-SHALISHA, a town in the land of Shalisha, signifying “lord of Shalisha.”

A man thence brought Elisha bread of the firstfruits and ears of corn.

Elisha bade his servant set it before an hundred men of the sons of the prophets.

They did eat, and left thereof, according to the word of the LORD.

It witnesses that the LORD multiplies the little brought to Him in faith.

📖 Key Scripture

2Ki 4:42 — "And there came a man from Baal-shalisha, and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in the husk thereof. And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat."

2Ki 4:44 — "So he set it before them, and they did eat, and left thereof, according to the word of the LORD."

1Sam 9:4 — "And he passed through mount Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalisha, but they found them not: then they passed through the land of Shalim, and there they were not: and he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but they found them not."

Joh 7:37 — "In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture; though its name bears the idol Baal, it witnesses that the LORD multiplies the firstfruits brought to Him in faith.

expand to see more

Baal-shalisha is a town of the land of Shalisha, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. Yet its very name preaches a real corruption of old: the name of Baal, the false god whose worship the LORD abhorred, was fastened even upon the towns of Israel, so deep had the plague of idolatry run in the land.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the LORD’s gracious provision and His honouring of faith, even in a place that bore an idol’s name. A man of Baal-shalisha brought the firstfruits of his ground unto the man of God, and the LORD multiplied the bread so that an hundred ate and left thereof. He who fed the prophets by Elisha is the same who fed the multitudes by His own hand, and who is Himself the bread of life. Where men turn from the dead Baal to the living God and bring Him their firstfruits, He fills the hungry and there is yet to spare.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “lord of Shalisha,” Baal-shalisha names the town whence firstfruits came to Elisha.

expand to see more

Baal-shalisha — Hebrew ba‘al shālīshāh, “lord of Shalisha.”

It lay in the land of Shalisha, near mount Ephraim.

Saul passed through that land seeking his father’s asses (1Sam 9:4).

A man thence brought Elisha the firstfruits of barley (2Ki 4:42).

The prophet fed an hundred men, and they left thereof (2Ki 4:44).

Usage

"Like the man of Baal-shalisha, the believer brings his firstfruits to God and sees them multiplied."

"The LORD is no man’s debtor, but fills the hungry and leaves yet to spare."

"Even from a place that bore an idol’s name, a faithful gift was honoured of the living God."
